top_choice_rationale: P002 (Helpman and Melitz, B005) has the most directly tested core mechanism. Selection into exporting and reallocation across heterogeneous firms have been confronted with firm-level and transaction-level data in many countries for over twenty years. The idea is mature and general, and it links trade to firm dynamics and aggregate productivity. The main weaknesses are attribution (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited), Helpman's marginal credit relative to Krugman's 2008 prize, and welfare results that depend on functional form. A citation anchored on the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection, and not on the empirical exporter-premium facts, manages these. P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore, B011) is a very close second. It has the cleaner two-author attribution and nearly three decades of use as a building block, but the collateral channel is identified more indirectly, and a citation would have to credit the mechanism and not a measured magnitude. P003 (B014) is a serious, well-replicated labour candidate. Its credit is harder to isolate because of the task and trade-shock strands, the omission of Dorn, Acemoglu and Restrepo, and the debated persistence of the China-shock effects. No award ranks last because each of the three proposals is a substantive, mature achievement. Vote counts in the round-2 slate are not treated as evidence of merit. This assessment rests on general knowledge and the supplied committee text, with no independent source verification.
recusal_note: Profile-based connections, disclosed and not adjudicated: frequent co-authorship with Per Krusell (secretary) and co-authorship with John Hassler (chair), both IIES colleagues and both supporters of P001, which I rank second. Long-running collaboration with Aghion, Bergeaud, Klenow and Li on creative destruction and growth measurement is thematically close to the firm-reallocation theme in P002 and could bias me toward it. I have no listed tie to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Hanson or Katz. Klenow is credited only in B016, which is not in the slate.
